div.head: Episc Inscr.
div.note: The Latin is the Quadripartitus; Liebermann's Old English is from X (Oxford, Bodleian, Junius 121, f. 13b, written at Worcester c. 1065). In OE the text survives only as a chapter in the middle of the so-called Polity (a compilation of c. 1027–60), but was perhaps originally separate, as the Quadripartitus had it. Liebermann dates it c. 1000–1050 and gives the German title in brackets as his own.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.1000–1050; ??(Whitelock); 1002x1008 (Rabin)”, now “c.1000–1050 (Liebermann); 1002×1008 (Rabin)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.1000–1050 (Liebermann); 1002×1008 (Rabin)”, now “c.1000–1050 (Liebermann, I p. 477); 1002×1008 (Rabin)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “X 477; Q 477; German 477”; 16 rows of Episc)

Preserved in Anglo-Saxon only as a chapter in the middle of the so-called Polity (ed. Thorpe Ancient laws p. 422, a compilation of c. 1027—60: on the religious and social duty of every rank, drawn from homilies, canons and laws), but perhaps originally a separate piece; Quadr. had it in that form
